topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic opens the lecture with welcoming remarks, connections to earlier practical work, and an overview of the planned learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor virology and the discovery of cellular oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the historical study of oncogenic viruses established that cancer originates from the misregulation or viral capture of normal cellular genes.

topics.label: Assays for measuring cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the in vitro and in vivo laboratory assays used to test whether candidate genes and specific mutations confer transformed properties on cells.

topics.label: Concepts and mutational mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes are categorized, how they regulate the G1/S cell cycle checkpoint, and how different classes of mutations affect their dominance and cellular function.

topics.label: Forms, causes, and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer, examining the specific failures in DNA repair pathways, replication fidelity, and mitosis that generate them.

topics.label: Multi-step genetic progression in the Vogelstein model
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how the sequential accumulation of mutations in oncogenes, tumor suppressor genes, and genomic maintenance pathways drives colorectal cancer progression.

topics.label: Hereditary cancer predisposition and tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how inherited germline mutations accelerate cancer development through the two-hit paradigm and how tumors subsequently evolve under therapeutic selective pressures.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by reviewing the covered learning outcomes, offering recommended reading, and outlining the next lecture topic.
